captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/5_jigsaw_puzzle, whose models/alexnet_jigsaw.py and data/jigsaw_dataset.py are the lab's own implementation of Noroozi & Favaro (2016), torch/torchvision only. So it ports self-contained (no third_party submodule), the treatment the other re-implemented methods received. The capture directory number (5) equals this method's number in the Step 1&2 list (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Unsupervised Learning of Visual Representations by Solving Jigsaw Puzzles

encoder: encoder.pt is the shared Context-Free Network (CFN) encoder (encoder.*): the AlexNet conv stack, the 1x1-conv CFN layers and the adaptive pool, producing a 512-d feature per tile/image. The permutation classifier (classifier.*) is pretext machinery and is excluded.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the CFN encoder's 512-d feature (images resized to the encoder's tile size), a genuine learned representation -- so the number is comparable. Follows the lab's ARSSL probe (L2-normalise + mean-centre, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5).
rewritten_during_the_port: the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the lab wrapper reached CUDA through DistributedDataParallel/setup_dist)
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss/accuracy and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and the TensorBoard logging so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged
the capture's step 2 (ViT jigsaw) is excluded, as in every port
